candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

Catalogue of proud kings whom God humbled — Re'aytawi (textually corrupt name, likely Pharaoh per Horovitz 1905 + crux-flag at CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX §1 Mq 5:1), Nimrod, and Nebuchadnezzar — each given as moral exemplar against pride. The Re'aytawi crux is philologically interesting: the closest Geʽez tradition is the Conflict of Adam and Eve with Satan (Geʽez Adambuch — Dillmann 1853 / Trumpp 1880 / Malan 1882) which uses comparable demonology-vocabulary. The chapter's homiletic pivot from narrative-martyrology to sustained-prophetic-indictment shapes the rest of 1 Mq's structure (chs. 5-36 are primarily homiletic-prophetic rather than narrative-martyrological).

candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

NIMROD — proud-tower-builder, humbled by God. The Genesis 11:1-9 Tower-of-Babel narrative names Nimrod (Gen 10:8-12) as the founder-of-Babel; Meqabyan integrates the Nimrod-tower tradition with the broader proud-king-humbled motif. The Nimrod-as-pride-exemplar reading parallels Josephus Antiquities 1.4.2 (Nimrod's tower 'designed to gain immortality and challenge God'); 3 Baruch 2-3 (the tower-builders punished); Pseudo-Philo Liber Antiquitatum Biblicarum 4.7 + 6.13 (the tower-builders dispersed). The verse establishes the second-fold in the chapter's catalog of humbled-kings (Re'aytawi-likely-Pharaoh in seed 5:1 → Nimrod-the-tower-builder → Nebuchadnezzar-humbled-to-beasts at 5:14) — a typological indictment of Ṣiruṣaydan's pride.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

NEBUCHADNEZZAR humbled-to-beasts — Daniel 4 directly cited. The Babylonian king's seven-year humiliation ('he was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till his hairs were grown like eagles' feathers, and his nails like birds' claws' — Dan 4:33) becomes the climactic exemplar of God's-judgment-on-proud-kings. The verse completes the chapter's tripartite humbled-king catalog and locates Ṣiruṣaydan's pride within the recurring biblical pattern. Meqabyan's distinctive contribution: the catalog-form of humbled-kings serves as PROPHETIC-WARNING addressed-to-Ṣiruṣaydan via the brothers' homiletic voice; the prophet-confronts-king pattern (Daniel-confronting-Nebuchadnezzar in Daniel 2 + Daniel 4) is preserved in this Meqabyan recapitulation.

NIMROD — proud-tower-builder, humbled by God. The Genesis 11:1-9 Tower-of-Babel narrative names Nimrod (Gen 10:8-12) as the founder-of-Babel; Meqabyan integrates the Nimrod-tower tradition with the broader proud-king-humbled motif. The Nimrod-as-pride-exemplar reading parallels Josephus Antiquities 1.4.2 (Nimrod's tower 'designed to gain immortality and challenge God'); 3 Baruch 2-3 (the tower-builders punished); Pseudo-Philo Liber Antiquitatum Biblicarum 4.7 + 6.13 (the tower-builders dispersed). The verse establishes the second-fold in the chapter's catalog of humbled-kings (Re'aytawi-likely-Pharaoh in seed 5:1 → Nimrod-the-tower-builder → Nebuchadnezzar-humbled-to-beasts at 5:14) — a typological indictment of Ṣiruṣaydan's pride.
